webHowItWorks:
The CosmetWiki web app is a light-only Next.js + Tailwind app with a distinctive dual visual language: (1) a "liquid-glass / glassmorphism" vocabulary for most content surfaces (translucent white over pastel background orbs), and (2) a "neumorphism / soft-UI" vocabulary for the home dashboard and certain CTAs (matte #E8ECF1 surfaces with dual light/dark shadows). Tokens are defined in three places and must all be honored together.

THEME LOCK (app/globals.css + app/layout.tsx):
- color-scheme is forced to "light only". `:root` declares neumorphism CSS vars: `--neu-bg: #e8ecf1`, `--neu-shadow-light: #ffffff`, `--neu-shadow-dark: #c5ccd6`.
- html/body base: background `#fafafa`, text color `#1f2937`, antialiased, text-rendering optimizeLegibility. A `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block FORCES the same light values with !important — dark mode is explicitly disabled. viewport themeColor is `#FAFAFA`, colorScheme "light".
- Text selection: background `rgba(244,63,94,0.2)` (rose-500 @20%), color `#1f2937`.
- IMPORTANT page-background switch: `body:has(.neu-page) { background: var(--neu-bg) }`. Pages that opt into the neumorphic stack add a `.neu-page` class to a top-level element, which flips the whole body background from #FAFAFA to #E8ECF1 so the neu shadows read correctly. The home dashboard does this.

TAILWIND TOKENS (tailwind.config.ts, theme.extend):
- colors: bg `#FAFAFA`; surface `#FFFFFF`; ink.DEFAULT `#1F2937`, ink.muted `#6B7280`, ink.subtle `#9CA3AF`; accent `#8B5CF6`, accentDark `#6D28D9`.
- rating scale (4 levels, each with DEFAULT/soft/ink): vert {DEFAULT #16A34A, soft #DCFCE7, ink #14532D}; jaune {#CA8A04, #FEF9C3, #713F12}; orange {#EA580C, #FFEDD5, #7C2D12}; rouge {#DC2626, #FEE2E2, #7F1D1D}.
- boxShadow named tokens: card `0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.05), 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.03)`; cardHover `0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.08), 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.04)`; search `0 4px 24px rgba(15,23,42,0.08), 0 2px 6px rgba(15,23,42,0.04)`; searchFocus `0 6px 32px rgba(244,63,94,0.18), 0 2px 8px rgba(15,23,42,0.08)`.
- fontFamily sans AND display both = [var(--font-inter), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif].
- animations: fade-in (200ms ease-out, translateY 2px→0), slide-down (220ms ease-out, translateY -6px→0), reveal (620ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) both, translateY 14px→0).

TYPOGRAPHY (app/layout.tsx): Inter from next/font/google, weights 400/500/600/700, subsets latin, display swap, exposed as CSS var `--font-inter`. There is NO separate display font — the same Inter is used for body and headings. Logo (components/Logo.tsx): "Cosme" in ink + "Check" in a `from-rose-400 to-pink-400` clip-text gradient; sizes sm=text-base/h-5, md=text-lg/h-6, lg=text-2xl/h-7; font-semibold tracking-tight; SVG flask icon stroke-width 1.8.

BACKGROUND GLOW (components/BackgroundGlow.tsx): pointer-events-none absolutely-positioned layer at -z-10, height min(100vh,900px), three large blur-3xl rounded-full orbs: (1) top-6% left-(-8%) 60vh×55vw gradient-to-br from-violet-200/35 via-fuchsia-100/25 to-pink-100/15; (2) top-10% right-(-8%) 55vh×55vw gradient-to-bl from-orange-100/35 via-rose-100/25 to-pink-100/15; (3) bottom-(-10%) left-8% 30vh×30vw gradient-to-tr from-purple-100/20 via-violet-50/12 to-transparent. Requires a `relative isolate` positioned ancestor.

GLASSMORPHISM (lib/ui/glass.ts) — these are the canonical surface recipes, exported as Tailwind class strings:
- GLASS_CARD: rounded-3xl (24px), bg-white/70, ring-1 ring-black/[0.06], backdrop-blur-2xl backdrop-saturate-150, shadow `0 4px 10px -2px rgba(15,23,42,0.08), 0 32px 64px -16px rgba(15,23,42,0.30), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.95), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(15,23,42,0.04)`.
- GLASS_CARD_HOVER: bg-white/80, shadow `0 6px 14px -2px rgba(15,23,42,0.10), 0 38px 72px -18px rgba(15,23,42,0.34)` + same insets.
- GLASS_PILL_CARD: rounded-[28px], bg-white/80, ring-1 ring-white/80, backdrop-blur-xl backdrop-saturate-150, shadow `0 18px 38px -14px rgba(15,23,42,0.18), 0 4px 10px -2px rgba(15,23,42,0.08)` + same insets. Hover lifts to `0 24px 48px -14px rgba(15,23,42,0.22)`.
- GLASS_PILL: rounded-full, bg-white/65, ring-1 ring-white/80, backdrop-blur-xl backdrop-saturate-150, shadow `0 8px 22px -8px rgba(15,23,42,0.16), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.9)`, hover bg-white/85.
- GLASS_CARD_DARK / GLASS_PILL_DARK (primary CTAs): bg gradient-to-br from-#1F2937 via-#111111 to-#0A0A0A, text-white, ring-1 ring-white/[0.08], shadow `0 22px 56px -18px rgba(15,23,42,0.45), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.10), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.30)` (pill: `0 14px 30px -12px`), hover:brightness-110.
- Tinted glass cards (rounded-3xl, gradient-to-br tint/85→tint/75, colored ring, backdrop-blur-2xl backdrop-saturate-150, colored 0 18px 48px -16px shadow + white insets): ROSE from-#FFE4E6/85 to-#FFF1F2/75 shadow rgba(244,63,94,0.18); AMBER amber-100/80→amber-50/70 shadow rgba(202,138,4,0.18); EMERALD emerald-100/80→emerald-50/70 shadow rgba(5,150,105,0.18); ORANGE orange-100/80→orange-50/70 shadow rgba(234,88,12,0.18); VIOLET violet-100/80→violet-50/70 shadow rgba(124,58,237,0.30).

NEUMORPHISM (globals.css @layer components) — all on var(--neu-bg) #E8ECF1 surface with dual shadows (dark #c5ccd6 bottom-right, light #ffffff top-left):
- .neu: radius 16px, shadow `6px 6px 14px dark, -6px -6px 14px light`. .neu-sm: radius 12px, `3px/8px`. .neu-sm-white / .neu-menu: white surface, same shadows (sm 12px, menu 14px radius).
- .neu-hover:hover: `8px 8px 18px / -8px -8px 18px`.
- .neu-inset: radius 12px, INSET `inset 4px 4px 9px dark, inset -4px -4px 9px light`. .neu-track (thin progress grooves ≤12px): `inset 2px 2px 4px / inset -2px -2px 4px`.
- .neu-btn: radius 12px, `4px 4px 9px / -4px -4px 9px`, font-weight 500, transition all .15s ease; hover `5px/11px`; active flips to inset `inset 3px 3px 6px / inset -3px -3px 6px`.
- .neu-btn-primary: bg linear-gradient(145deg, #9b6ef5, #7c3aed), white text, font-weight 600, shadow `4px 4px 9px dark, -2px -2px 6px light`; hover translateY(-1px); active translateY(0) + `inset 2px 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,0.25)`.
- .neu-shadow (colored-pill lift, stronger): `8px 8px 16px rgba(163,177,198,0.55), -6px -6px 14px rgba(255,255,255,0.85)`; hover `10px/0.6 + translateY(-1px)`; active `inset 3px 3px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.25)`. Variants: .neu-shadow-blue drop `rgba(79,70,229,0.5)` active inset `rgba(40,30,120,0.35)`; .neu-shadow-rose drop `rgba(244,63,94,0.45)` active inset `rgba(120,20,40,0.4)`.
- Tinted neu: .neu-rose bg linear-gradient(135deg,#FFE4E6,#FFF1F2); .neu-amber bg linear-gradient(135deg,#FEF3C7,#FFFBEB) — both radius 16px with the standard 6px neu dual shadow.
- HomeDashboard inline neu tiles use gradients: violet tile `linear-gradient(135deg,#6C3FD8 0%,#4F46E5 55%,#7C3AED 100%)`; green tile `linear-gradient(135deg,#D6F5D6 0%,#E8FAE8 50%,#C8F0C8 100%)`, both with the standard neu box-shadow.

OTHER RECIPES:
- .surface: white, radius 16px, shadow `0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.05), 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.03)`.
- .gradient-text: linear-gradient(135deg, #8b5cf6 0%, #ec4899 50%, #f97316 100%) clipped to text.
- Rating gradients (lib/colors.ts RATING_GRADIENT, Tailwind from/via/to): Vert from-emerald-500 via-green-500 to-teal-500; Jaune from-amber-400 via-yellow-500 to-orange-400; Orange from-orange-500 via-orange-600 to-red-500; Rouge from-red-500 via-rose-600 to-pink-600. RATING_CLASS chips use bg-{rating}-soft text-{rating}-ink ring-1 ring-{rating}/20-30.
- Rose/pink primary button recipe (search/scan CTAs): bg gradient from-rose-500 to-pink-500 (or 400 for secondary), white, shadow `0 4px 14px -4px rgba(244,63,94,0.45), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.30)`, hover from-rose-600/to-pink-600.
- FAB (center nav, AppShell): 64px (w-16 h-16) rounded-full bg gradient-to-br from-rose-400 to-pink-500, white, ring-4 ring-white/70, shadow `0 8px 22px -6px rgba(244,63,94,0.55), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.55)`, active:scale-95.
- CreditsPill: dark bg gradient-to-br from-zinc-800 to-black, ring-1 ring-amber-400/30, gold inner badge gradient from-amber-300 to-amber-500.
- Tab bar / sticky headers: bg-white/80 backdrop-blur-md border-b border-black/[0.06]. Modals: fixed overlay bg-black/40 backdrop-blur-sm.

ANIMATIONS (globals.css keyframes): hero-underline-draw (SVG stroke-dashoffset 220→0, 900ms 350ms cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)); shimmer (translateX -100%→400%); reveal-anim (.reveal-on-mount opacity+translateY(20px)→0, 900ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), with delay utility classes 100/150/160/220/270/320ms); blob-pop-anim (.blob-pop-in scale 0.55→1 with overshoot cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1), 720ms, transform-origin 50% 60%); stagger-up-anim (.stagger-up opacity+translateY(12px)→0, 520ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), inline --stagger-delay). All three reveal/blob/stagger animations are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. grain-overlay utility = SVG fractalNoise feTurbulence baseFrequency 0.85, 240×240 tile.

BORDER-RADIUS SCALE in use: 8px (neu-sm-ish small), 12px (neu-sm, neu-inset, neu-btn, neu-menu), 16px (neu, surface, neu-rose/amber = Tailwind rounded-2xl), 24px (rounded-3xl = GLASS_CARD), 28px (rounded-[28px] = GLASS_PILL_CARD), full/9999 (pills, FAB). Glass content cards commonly use rounded-2xl (16px) for inner articles and rounded-3xl (24px) for big panels.

nativeMobilePlan:
Most of this is ALREADY built in the mobile app — do not rebuild from scratch, extend the existing files. constants/colors.ts already mirrors the web tokens (bg #FAFAFA, surface #FFF, ink #1F2937/inkMuted #6B7280/inkLight #9CA3AF, accent #8B5CF6/accentDeep #7C3AED, rose #F43F5E, rating vert/jaune/orange/rouge, neu {bg #E8ECF1, shadowDark #C5CCD6, shadowLight #FFF}, glass {bg rgba(255,255,255,0.7), bgStrong 0.9, border rgba(0,0,0,0.06)}). constants/spacing.ts has the radius scale. components/design/NeuCard.tsx and GlassCard.tsx implement the two surface languages.

GAPS TO CLOSE for pixel-parity:
1. Color tokens: add accentDark #6D28D9, ink ring-soft rgba(0,0,0,0.06) already present; add rating `ink` colors (vert #14532D, jaune #713F12, orange #7C2D12, rouge #7F1D1D) — current mobile colors.ts only has text+bg, missing the dark ink chip text. Add roseDeep alias matches web pink-600 family. Add the gradient-text stops (#8b5cf6/#ec4899/#f97316) and rating gradient stops for use with expo-linear-gradient.
2. Shadows: RN can only render ONE shadow per View. The existing NeuCard already solves dual-shadow via nested Views (light shadow outer, dark shadow inner) on iOS + elevation on Android. For glass multi-layer shadows (GLASS_CARD has up to 4 stacked shadows incl. insets), RN cannot do inset shadows or multiple drop shadows natively — approximate: use the largest drop shadow (e.g. 0 32px 64px -16px rgba(15,23,42,0.30) → shadowOffset {0,16}, shadowRadius 32, shadowOpacity ~0.18, shadowColor #0F172A) and fake the inset top highlight with a 1px top borderColor rgba(255,255,255,0.95) or a thin top-edge View. Consider react-native-shadow-2 for closer multi-shadow control if needed.
3. Blur: GlassCard already uses expo-blur BlurView (intensity ~20 maps to backdrop-blur-2xl; bump intensity for blur-2xl vs blur-md; tint='light'). Android fallback raises bg opacity to >=0.92 — keep that.
4. Background orbs: build a BackgroundGlow RN component using expo-linear-gradient inside absolutely-positioned rounded Views, then apply heavy blur. Native blur on large gradient Views is expensive — better approach: pre-render the three-orb glow as a single static PNG/WEBP asset (export from web) and use it as a background Image, OR use expo-linear-gradient ellipses with low opacity and skip the blur. The orbs are decorative and low-opacity (12-35%) so a baked image is the safest pixel-match.
5. Gradients: use expo-linear-gradient for all from/via/to gradients — neu-btn-primary (145deg #9b6ef5→#7c3aed), rose CTA (from-rose-500 #F43F5E→pink-500), FAB (from-rose-400→pink-500), dark glass (#1F2937→#111111→#0A0A0A), rating gradients, gradient-text (use MaskedView + LinearGradient for clip-text, or react-native-linear-gradient text mask). Note RN gradients use `colors` array + `start/end` points rather than CSS angles — convert 135deg to start {0,0} end {1,1}, 145deg approx the same, to-r to start {0,0.5} end {1,0.5}, to-br start {0,0} end {1,1}, to-bl start {1,0} end {0,1}.
6. Typography: install Inter via expo-font/@expo-google-fonts/inter (weights 400/500/600/700). Build a Text wrapper or theme that defaults to Inter. No separate display font needed (web reuses Inter). Logo: MaskedView + LinearGradient (rose-400→pink-400) over the 'Check' word; ink 'Cosme'.
7. Animations: use react-native-reanimated (already a dependency) to port reveal (translateY 20→0 + opacity, 900ms, easing bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)), stagger-up (12→0, 520ms), blob-pop (scale 0.55→1 overshoot bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1), 720ms). Use withTiming + Easing.bezier. Respect reduced-motion via AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled.
8. neu-page background switch: on screens that use neumorphic cards, set the screen container backgroundColor to colors.neu.bg (#E8ECF1) instead of bg (#FAFAFA), matching web's body:has(.neu-page) rule.
9. Add tinted neu/glass variants (rose/amber/emerald/orange/violet) as props/variants on NeuCard/GlassCard, plus a dark-glass variant for primary CTAs.
10. Selection/themeColor: set Expo statusBar style light content as appropriate; selection color rose@20% maps to TextInput selectionColor rgba(244,63,94,0.2).

webHowItWorks:
The web app's chrome is centralized in `components/nav/AppShell.tsx`, a single client component mounted once in `app/layout.tsx` wrapping all authenticated pages. It receives `signedIn`, `firstName`, `initialCredits` (SSR-prefetched) and `hideOnPaths` (["/auth","/scan/photo","/onboarding"]). It short-circuits to bare `{children}` when the path is hidden or the user is signed out.

NAV MODEL: a single `NAV_ITEMS` array (7 entries) drives every surface: `/` Accueil (HomeIcon), `/routine` Routine (LayersIcon), `/promesses` Promesses (PromisesIcon), `/advisor` Beauty Advisor (SparklesIcon), `/history` Historique (ClockIcon), `/offre` Offre (DiamondIcon), `/profile` Profil (UserIcon). Desktop sidebar shows all 7; mobile bottom nav shows only 4 + the center FAB; the burger drawer shows all 7 plus credits/premium/logout.

MOBILE BOTTOM NAV (`MobileBottomNav` inside AppShell.tsx): a fixed `<nav>` at `bottom-0 inset-x-0 z-[80]`, `lg:hidden`, `pointer-events-none` on the wrapper with `pointer-events-auto` re-enabled on the inner pill, padded `pb-[max(env(safe-area-inset-bottom),12px)] pt-2 px-3`. Inner pill: `mx-auto max-w-md`, `flex items-end justify-between rounded-full`, background `bg-gradient-to-b from-[#FFE4E6]/85 to-[#FFD1DC]/75` (rose/pink top-to-bottom), `backdrop-blur-2xl`, `ring-1 ring-white/70`, shadow `0_10px_30px_-12px_rgba(244,63,94,0.25)` + inset highlight `inset_0_1px_0_rgba(255,255,255,0.75)`, `px-3 py-1.5`. Only 4 nav items render in the pill (Accueil, Routine, then a spacer, Historique, Promesses) — NOT all 7. A `<div className="w-16 h-16">` spacer sits dead-center to reserve room for the FAB.

ACTIVE-ITEM (NavBtnMobile): each item is a Link, `flex flex-col items-center gap-0.5 py-1.5 px-1 w-14 text-[10px] font-medium`. Active text color `#F43F5E`, inactive `#4B5563`. The icon sits in an inner `h-8 w-8 rounded-full` span; when active it gets a neumorphic frosted pill: `background:#FFD1DC` with dual shadow `3px 3px 6px #E8A8B4, -3px -3px 6px #FFF0F3` (dark bottom-right + light top-left = raised pink). Icons are 20px (`h-5 w-5`). Active label becomes `font-semibold`.

CENTER FAB "Décode": absolutely positioned `left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -top-6` so it overhangs the pill top by 24px. Size `w-16 h-16` (64px) `rounded-full`, gradient `bg-gradient-to-br from-rose-400 to-pink-500`, white content, `flex flex-col items-center justify-center gap-0.5`, `ring-4 ring-white/70` (thick white ring), shadow `0_8px_22px_-6px_rgba(244,63,94,0.55)` + inset highlight. Contents: CameraIcon `h-5 w-5 drop-shadow-sm` over a `text-[10px] font-semibold` label reading "Décode". Interactions: `active:scale-95 hover:brightness-105`. It does NOT navigate — it calls `handleScanClick`, which checks credits (if remaining<=0 dispatches `cosmecheck:credits-exhausted` and aborts) then opens the ScanSheet modal.

FLOATING ADVISOR BUTTON: separate from the nav — a `lg:hidden fixed right-4 z-[75] h-12 w-12 rounded-full` dark-gradient button (`from-[#1F2937] via-[#111111] to-[#0A0A0A]`) with a gold (`#FBBF24`) SparklesIcon, positioned `bottom: calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 88px)` (floats above the bar), hidden on /advisor.

BURGER DRAWER (`MobileBurgerMenu.tsx`): floating button `lg:hidden fixed top-3 right-3 z-40 h-11 w-11 rounded-full bg-white/85 backdrop-blur-md ring-1 ring-black/[0.06]` with MenuIcon. Opens a `fixed inset-0 z-[90]` overlay: dimmed backdrop `bg-black/45` (tap to close) + right-side drawer `absolute top-0 right-0 h-full w-[78%] max-w-[320px] bg-[#FAFAFA]` with shadow `-12px_0_40px_-8px`, animated via `@keyframes slideInRight translateX(100%)→0` (220ms) and backdrop `fadeIn` (180ms). Header: "Cosme Check" wordmark (black "Cosme " + rose "Check") + CloseIcon button. Scrollable nav lists ALL 7 NAV_ITEMS as `rounded-2xl px-3.5 py-3 text-[14px]` rows; active row `bg-white font-semibold ring-1 ring-black/[0.06]` + soft shadow, inactive `text-[#4B5563] hover:bg-black/[0.04]`. Pinned bottom block (`mt-auto`): credits card ("Vos crédits restants" + CreditsPill), PremiumCard (hidden on /offre), and a "Se déconnecter" form button (`bg-rose-50 text-rose-700 ring-rose-200`). Body scroll-locked while open; closes on Escape, on route change (pathname effect), and on backdrop tap.

SCAN SHEET (`ScanSheet.tsx`): bottom sheet on mobile (`items-end`, `rounded-t-3xl`, grab handle `h-1 w-10 bg-[#D1D5DB]`), centered modal on desktop. Backdrop `bg-[rgba(17,17,17,0.45)]`, `z-[100]`, animates `fadeIn`/`slideUp`. Has a 5-state machine (picker/paste/search/barcode/url). Picker is an asymmetric 2+3 grid: left column 2 large square tiles (Code-barres→inline barcode view, Photo→routes to /scan/photo), right column 3 compact tiles (Coller la composition, Coller le lien [NEW badge], Rechercher un produit→/produits). On submit it stashes INCI in sessionStorage (`cw:pendingInci`) + optional product source (`cw:pendingProductSource`), paints a ProcessingOverlay, and `router.push("/analyse?inci=...")`. Heading is `text-[20px] font-bold text-[#1E3A8A]` (navy). Opening can also be triggered anywhere via the `cosmecheck:open-scan` DOM event.

ICONS (`NavIcons.tsx`): inline stroke-only SVGs, `viewBox 0 0 24 24`, `strokeWidth 1.8`, round caps/joins, `currentColor`. Set: Home, Layers, Clock, User, Camera, Barcode, Clipboard, Search, Sparkles, Promises (clipboard+tick), Menu, Close, Link, Diamond.

webHowItWorks:
There are THREE distinct visual components here, two of which are donut/arc gauges and one of which is an icon meter. They do NOT share code.

== 1. IngredientBlob (components/blob/IngredientBlob.tsx) — the flagship organic half-donut ==
This is a 180-degree half-ring (donut hollow) split into up to 4 angular sectors, one per color category (vert/jaune/orange/rouge), where the radial boundaries between sectors are deformed into wavy "blob" edges. It is the primary distribution viz on the analyse page.

GEOMETRY (all in viewBox units, y-DOWN coordinate system). Three variants live in a GEOMETRY record:
- lg: width 520, height 290, cx 240, cy 240, rOuter 220, rInner 90, jitter 0.07, edgeSegments 16, roundStroke 18, gapAngle 0.11
- md: width 280, height 152, cx 128, cy 124, rOuter 116, rInner 46, jitter 0.06, edgeSegments 12, roundStroke 9, gapAngle 0.10
- sm: width 64, height 38, cx 28, cy 32, rOuter 28, rInner 12, jitter 0.04, edgeSegments 8, roundStroke 3, gapAngle 0.10
The center (cx,cy) sits near the BOTTOM of the viewBox; the ring bulges UPWARD. The viewBox is wider than tall so only the top half-ring shows.

ANGLE MODEL: angles run from -PI (far left, pointing left along the flat base) sweeping clockwise to 0 (far right). Points are computed as x = cx + r*cos(angle), y = cy + r*sin(angle). Because y is down, sin over [-PI,0] is negative, so the arc lies above cy.

SLICE COMPUTATION (computeSlices): total = sum of 4 counts. minAngle = PI*0.04 (~7.2deg). If total===0, the 4 colors get an equal PI/4 split (ring never empty). Otherwise only colors with count>0 are present; each present color gets angle = (count/total)*PI. Any present slice below minAngle is floored to minAngle and the surplus is taken pro-rata from the larger slices (reserved = small.length*minAngle; bigSum = sum of >=minAngle angles; remain = PI - reserved; big slices rescaled by remain/bigSum). Cursor starts at -PI and accumulates, emitting {color,start,end} per slice.

INTER-SLICE GAP: half = gapAngle/2. Every internal junction loses gapAngle total, half from each side: slice i start += half (unless first), end -= half (unless last). The far-left/far-right ends stay flush on the flat base (no neighbor there). This leaves a clean background-colored groove between slices.

EDGES (lib/blob/path.ts): each slice gets its OWN left+right radial edge (adjacent slices no longer share an edge — that is what creates the visible gap):
- The first slice's left edge and the last slice's right edge are straightRadialEdge: sample edgeSegments+1 points linearly in radius from rInner to rOuter at a fixed angle.
- All internal edges are wavyRadialEdge: same radial sampling but each point's ANGLE is jittered by (rng()-0.5)*2*jitter*sin(t*PI). The sin(PI*t) envelope forces jitter to zero at both rInner and rOuter so wavy edges still meet the clean inner/outer arcs exactly. RNG is mulberry32(seed) — a deterministic 32-bit PRNG. The two edges flanking the SAME junction use the SAME seed (JUNCTION_SEEDS = [10133, 24517, 38981], indexed so junction i uses sliceEdges right of slice i and left of slice i+1) so the two wavy silhouettes mirror and the groove stays constant-width. Per-color fallback seeds SEEDS = {vert:8721, jaune:4193, orange:6504, rouge:2876}.

PATH BUILD (ringSectorPath): M to leftEdge[0]; L through all leftEdge points (inner->outer); outer arc `A rOuter rOuter 0 0 1 <rightEdge.last>` (sweep clockwise); L back through rightEdge points reversed (outer->inner); inner arc `A rInner rInner 0 0 0 <leftEdge[0]>` (sweep counter-clockwise); Z. All coords are toFixed(2).

COLORS (fill): vert #A3D26C, jaune #F6CE5A, orange #F49B43, rouge #E0432A. Each <path> uses fill = its color AND stroke = the SAME color with strokeWidth = roundStroke, strokeLinejoin/Linecap = round. The same-color round stroke is the "pill morphism" trick: it rounds every corner (radial-edge meets arc) and the wavy edges themselves, turning a sharp sector into a soft blob. The gap lets the wide stroke spill outward without bleeding into a neighbor.

NEUMORPHIC MODE (neumorphic prop): swaps the single group claymorphism shadow for a dual neumorphic shadow. The whole SVG gets a white top-left highlight filter: drop-shadow(-4px -4px 7px var(--neu-shadow-light)) where --neu-shadow-light = #ffffff. Then EACH slice <path> gets its OWN colored dark shadow via per-path CSS filter drop-shadow(dx dy blur COLOR) where the shadow color is a darker tint of the slice color: BLOB_SHADOW = {vert rgba(123,176,67,0.7), jaune rgba(214,165,44,0.68), orange rgba(214,118,40,0.68), rouge rgba(190,52,28,0.68)}. Per-variant offsets NEU_SLICE_SHADOW = {lg {dx3,dy9,blur13}, md {dx1.5,dy5,blur7}, sm {dx0.5,dy1.8,blur2.5}} (in viewBox units). When NOT neumorphic, the <g> wrapping all slices gets a neutral group shadow geom.shadow (e.g. lg: "drop-shadow(0 6px 10px rgba(15,23,42,0.10)) drop-shadow(0 2px 3px rgba(15,23,42,0.06))").

CENTER TEXT (showCenter): centerY = cy - rInner*0.55. Two SVG <text> centered: the total count (fontSize 56 lg / 28 else, weight 700, fill #1F2937) and the word "ingrédients" below it at centerY + (30 lg / 18 else) (fontSize 16 lg / 11 else, fill #6B7280).

LEGEND: two layouts. "below" (default) = 4-col grid of mini organic-blob swatches (blobPath = organicBlob, a Catmull-Rom closed blob of 11 points), each with count/total and an italic label (BLOB_LABEL = sans pénalité / pénalité faible / pénalité moyenne / pénalité forte) colored with BLOB_TEXT (vert #84B043, jaune #D4A017, orange #E07F2C, rouge #C73523). "around" = 3-col CSS grid placing jaune/orange labels top and vert/rouge labels bottom around the centered SVG (uses AroundLabel with BLOB_PLURAL = verts/jaunes/oranges/rouges).

ANIMATION (animate prop): adds class blob-pop-in. CSS keyframes blob-pop-anim: 720ms cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) both, transform-origin 50% 60%, transform-box fill-box; 0% {opacity 0, scale 0.55} -> 60% {opacity 1} -> 100% {opacity 1, scale 1}. The >1 overshoot in the bezier gives a small bounce. Respects prefers-reduced-motion (no animation).

== 2. HalfDonut (components/features/HalfDonut.tsx) — simple stroked half-donut ==
A much simpler 180-degree gauge that draws 4 colored arc strokes on a track. Props: vert/jaune/orange/rouge, size=160, thickness=18. Returns null if total<=0. cx=cy=size/2, r=(size-thickness)/2. viewBox `0 0 size size/2+thickness/2`. Segments order vert/jaune/orange/rouge with HARD colors: vert #10B981, jaune #FBBF24, orange #F97316, rouge #F43F5E (different palette from IngredientBlob). Each present segment: start = (acc/total)*180, end = ((acc+value)/total)*180, then startAngle = 180-start, endAngle = 180-end (so it sweeps left->right). Endpoints x = cx + r*cos(deg2rad), y = cy - r*sin(deg2rad) (note MINUS for y — y-up convention here). Path is a single arc `M x1 y1 A r r 0 large 1 x2 y2`, large = (end-start>180)?1:0 (always 0 for a half donut). A background track is drawn first: `M thickness/2 cy A r r 0 0 1 size-thickness/2 cy`, stroke #F3F4F6, strokeLinecap round. Colored arcs use strokeWidth=thickness, strokeLinecap=butt (no rounded caps, so segments butt against each other). Below the SVG: a row of 4 Dot legend items (2x2px dot + count). No animation, no neumorphism.

== 3. VerdictGauge (components/analyse/VerdictGauge.tsx) — NOT a donut, an icon meter ==
This is a horizontal/vertical row of 5 circular "pastilles" (icon badges), NOT an arc gauge. It is a "use client" component. Props: tone (VerdictTone), orientation horizontal|vertical, className. SLOTS array of 5: very-safe (HeartIcon, bg-emerald-400 active / bg-emerald-100 inactive), safe (LeafIcon, emerald), caution (EyeIcon, amber-400/amber-100), warning (AlertTriangleIcon, orange-500/orange-100), danger (StopOctagonIcon, rose-500/rose-100). ACTIVE_INDEX_BY_TONE maps tone->index (very-safe 0 ... danger 4, high-risk shares 4, unknown -1). Each slot is a stable h-9 w-9 box. The active pastille is h-12 w-12 with ring-4 ring-white + a saturated bg + shadow-[0_10px_24px_-6px_rgba(15,23,42,0.45)] + z-10, intentionally overflowing its slot (parent has overflow-visible) to look like a lifted 3D badge. Inactive pastilles are h-7 w-7 with pale bg + saturate-50 + opacity-40. Icons are inline SVGs (Heart/Leaf/Eye/AlertTriangle/StopOctagon) drawn with currentColor; size h-5 w-5 active / h-4 w-4 inactive. transition-all duration-200. Has role=meter with aria-valuemin/max/now. NOTE: this component has nothing to do with SVG arc geometry — it is icon pastilles styled with Tailwind.

== Shared geometry library (lib/blob/path.ts) ==
Used only by IngredientBlob. Exports mulberry32 (deterministic PRNG), wavyRadialEdge, straightRadialEdge, ringSectorPath, organicBlob (alias blobPath), type Pt. Pure TS with no DOM/React dependency — directly portable to React Native.

webHowItWorks:
The web app (D:\MesApps\deploy\CosmetWiki, Next.js App Router) exposes 4 entry points into the analysis pipeline, all of which converge on producing an INCI string that is handed off to /analyse via sessionStorage. There are NO Supabase Edge Functions in the web project; all server logic lives in Next.js API routes (runtime "nodejs", force-dynamic) that call OpenAI directly and scrape/query public sources. The mobile app must replicate this server logic as Supabase Edge Functions because mobile cannot embed the OpenAI key or run server-only libs (sharp, tesseract).

ENTRY POINT ORCHESTRATION (components/nav/ScanSheet.tsx): A bottom-sheet modal with an asymmetric tile picker. LEFT_TILES = physical-product flows: "Code-barres" (inline view -> BarcodeScannerInput) and "Photo de la composition" (routes to /scan/photo -> PhotoOcrFlow). RIGHT_TILES = data-only flows: "Coller la composition" (paste INCI), "Coller le lien" (URL), "Rechercher un produit" (routes to /produits). On submit, ALL flows call submitForAnalysis(): trims INCI, stashes it under sessionStorage key "cw:pendingInci" (authoritative handoff because Next.js prefetched shells can drop the URL searchParam), optionally stashes brand/name/source/ean under "cw:pendingProductSource", paints a ProcessingOverlay bridge, then router.push(`/analyse?inci=...`). It prefetches /analyse on open so the overlay paints in the same frame as navigation.

1) BARCODE SCANNING (components/BarcodeScannerInput.tsx, lazy-loaded ssr:false ~80kb): On mount it requests getUserMedia({video:{facingMode:{ideal:"environment"}}}). Handles secure-context, permission-denied (with per-platform iOS/Android/desktop unblock instructions), no-camera, unsupported. Decoder strategy: prefers native window.BarcodeDetector (Chrome/Edge/Android) with formats ean_13, ean_8, upc_a, upc_e, qr_code, code_128, polled via requestAnimationFrame; falls back to @zxing/browser BrowserMultiFormatReader (Safari iOS, Firefox). On a detected raw value it client-side gates with BARCODE_RE = /^\d{8,14}$/ (drops QR URLs/IMEIs without burning an API call), fires navigator.vibrate(80), then POSTs { barcode } to /api/product-by-barcode. found -> onFound({ingredientsText,brand,productName,source,sourceUrl,ean}); not-found -> recovery panel offering "Chercher par nom" / "Coller la liste INCI" / "Scanner un autre code". A detectedRef gate prevents duplicate lookups; resumeDetectionRef restarts the loop on retry.

   /api/product-by-barcode (app/api/product-by-barcode/route.ts, nodejs, maxDuration 30): IP rate-limit 20/60s, honeypot field "hp" -> blacklist+403, validates BARCODE_RE. Lookup ladder: (1) fetch OBF (world.openbeautyfacts.org) AND OPF (world.openproductsfacts.org) /api/v2/product/{barcode}.json in parallel (8s timeout, custom User-Agent), prefer OBF if its ingredients_text >=30 chars, else OPF; on a hit with looksLikeInci()==true it fire-and-forgets upsertCatalogProduct() into the catalog. (2) If a DB has a name but no INCI -> run searchProductCascade(brand+name) and prefer the barcode-DB brand/name. (3) If barcode totally unknown -> searchProductByBarcode() = GPT web-search last resort. (4) NOT_FOUND. Returns ProductSearchResult { found, brand, productName, ingredientsText, source, sourceUrl, confidence }.

2) PHOTO OCR PIPELINE (app/scan/photo/page.tsx -> components/scan/PhotoOcrFlow.tsx): Two-photo capture UI (front="Devant" optional for identity, back="Dos" required for INCI), file inputs with accept="image/*", blob-URL previews. process(): builds FormData (image_back required, image_front optional) and POSTs to /api/ocr via apiFetch. On success extracts data.text (INCI) and data.front {productName,brand,productType}. FALLBACK: if server OCR returns nothing, dynamically imports tesseract.js and runs Tesseract.recognize(backFile, "eng+fra") client-side. Then quickInciSanityCheck(text) gates before navigating: if it doesn't look like INCI -> "no_inci" recovery screen with photo tips + paste fallback. On pass -> handoff() stashes INCI + front identity (source="photo") in sessionStorage and routes to /analyse.

   /api/ocr (app/api/ocr/route.ts, nodejs, maxDuration 25): apiGate (auth + per-user "ocr" feature gating/credits). Reads multipart formData (image_back alias image, optional image_front). Validates MIME (jpeg/png/webp/heic/heif) and size (<=6MB). Runs ocrFromImageBase64 (back) and ocrFrontFromImageBase64 (front) in parallel.

   lib/ai/ocr.ts (the heavy logic): Back-label OCR: SHA-256 cache by image bytes; downscaleImage() via lazy sharp to 1600px/JPEG-85 (cuts vision tokens 50-70%); locateInciRegion() = cheap low-detail GPT-4o-mini Vision call returning a normalized bbox of the INGREDIENTS block, then cropToBbox() (sharp extract, 5% pad) to strip multilingual descriptive paragraphs; main OCR is GPT-4o-mini Vision (detail "high", temperature 0, JSON response) with a strict French system prompt ("N'INVENTE JAMAIS", only the INGREDIENTS/INCI/COMPOSITION block, ignore Nordic/Germanic descriptive text) returning {found,text,uncertain[]}. validateOcrText() parses tokens (parseInciList) and matches them against the live INCI DB via RPC cosme_check_match_inci_batch, returning a confidence level (ok >=0.70, low_match 0.30-0.70, very_low_match <0.30) with a French nudge message. A conditional SECOND PASS (ocrSecondPass) runs only when token count is 6-17 AND match rate <0.70, asking Vision for only the missing ingredients and merging. Everything is wrapped in callWithFallback (feature "ocr", credit/usage tracking); if OpenAI is unavailable it returns reason so the browser falls back to Tesseract. Front OCR (ocrFrontFromImageBase64): single GPT-4o-mini Vision call extracting {brand, productName, productType} for product identity; all-null treated as failure.

3) PRODUCT SEARCH / LOOKUP CASCADE (lib/productSearch/cascade.ts -> searchProductCascade): Global 8s timeout (Vercel Hobby 10s cap). Step 0: own catalog searchCatalogByName (Postgres, sub-100ms). Step 1: Supabase product cache getProductCache(queryNorm), re-validated against the query via matchesQuery() so historical bad matches self-heal. Step 2: fire OBF + INCIDecoder + optional brand-specific scraper + DuckDuckGo+Mistral in parallel (Promise.allSettled), pick first matching hit in priority order, fire-and-forget setProductCache. Sources: openBeautyFacts.ts (searchOpenBeautyFacts uses the cgi/search.pl endpoint, picks fr>generic>en name/ingredients, requires ingredients >30 chars and a token-overlap match, returns OBF product URL); inciDecoder.ts (searchInciDecoder: scrape search page -> first /products/{slug} -> fetch product HTML -> extract title/brand -> extractInciFromHtml via Mistral; also searchInciDecoderList for disambiguation lists and fetchInciDecoderProduct for lazy per-slug INCI). 

   /api/product-search (POST, nodejs, rate-limit 20/60s): runs normalizeProductQuery (GPT-4o-mini: detects barcodes pasted into name field, typos, ambiguity -> returns kind barcode|candidates|query). If query -> searchProductCascade; when cascade misses, collectOpenAIWebCandidates (primary, reliable from Vercel IPs) falling back to collectDuckDuckGoCandidates (free but bot-walled), then prevalidateCandidates extracts INCI per candidate in parallel and keeps only clickable ones (VALIDATED_TARGET=8). Supports infinite pagination via exclude[] ("Voir plus", FIRST_BATCH_LIMIT=24).

   /api/product-suggest (GET, cacheable via Cache-Control s-maxage=300, rate-limit 30/60s): the autocomplete/disambiguation list. Merges catalog (RPC cosme_check_search_catalog with pre-computed scores) > Supabase product_inci_cache (cosme_check schema, ilike) > OBF list > INCIDecoder list, deduped by dedupeKey (first 6 sorted normalized tokens). Catalog hits carry score/scoreLabel/scoreTone. Web fallback (OpenAI then DDG, prevalidated) only attaches when merged.length < 5. INCIDecoder candidates ship empty INCI (slug present) and are lazy-fetched on click.

4) INCI EXTRACTION: Three mechanisms. (a) From structured DBs: OBF/OPF ingredients_text fields directly. (b) From HTML pages: extractInciFromHtml (Mistral) used by INCIDecoder + DDG candidate prevalidation. (c) From images: GPT-4o-mini Vision in lib/ai/ocr.ts (bbox-crop + multi-pass) with Tesseract.js as a client-side fallback. The looksLikeInci() heuristic (>=5 comma/semicolon tokens, avg token length <=40) gates DB writes; quickInciSanityCheck() gates photo handoff client-side; validateOcrText() against cosme_check_match_inci_batch RPC scores OCR confidence.

   - exposureScore /20 (higher = safer): for each product penaltyPerUse = max(0, 20 - score); routine score = 20 - sum(penaltyPerUse × freqWeight) / max(totalUnits, eps), clamped 0..20. webHowItWorks:
The PROMESSES feature compares a product's marketing claims ("promesses") against its real INCI formula and produces a per-promise verdict ladder, a global % score, bar charts, a marketing index, an ingredient-position chart, and an LLM-written conclusion. Anti-hallucination is structural: the LLM only PROPOSES which actives would support a claim; a deterministic engine MECHANICALLY checks whether those actives are physically in the formula. The LLM can never inject an ingredient that isn't in the analyse.

DATA MODEL
- Parent: cosme_check.analyses (an INCI analysis with result_json: AnalyseResponse {items[], counts, score...}). Each item has position, slug, name, colorRating (Vert/Jaune/Orange/Rouge), tags[], thresholdContext ("after_fragrance"|"after_preservative").
- Child: cosme_check.coherence_analyses {id, user_id, analysis_id (FK), description, result_json: CoherenceResult, created_at}. RLS scopes rows to the user.

THE WIZARD (components/coherence/CoherenceWizard.tsx, client) — 3 steps + transient "running":
1. "Description": textarea for the marketing copy. Min 30 / max 6000 chars, live counter.
2. "Produit": pick mode tabs — "Depuis l'historique" (list of the user's saved analyses, single-select, rose highlight + check) OR "Coller une liste INCI" (name + INCI textarea; min 20 / max 12000). Paste mode calls POST /api/analyser first to create+save a real analyse row (costs 1 credit), then promotes it as the selected option. A banner warns paste = 2 credits total.
3. "Vérification": shows selected product card (title, matched/total ingredients, top-3, vert/jaune/orange/rouge distribution dots) with a warning that a mismatched INCI gives wrong results.
A clickable Stepper (numbered → green ✓ when reached) lets the user jump back to visited steps. Pre-fill flow: arriving via ?analysisId=&description= (from PromesseFlowModal) marks steps as reached up-front and lands on Description so the user can sanity-check the web-fetched description. "Lancer l'analyse" POSTs /api/coherence and router.push(`/promesses/${id}`).

THE PIPELINE (app/api/coherence/route.ts, runtime nodejs, maxDuration 25, force-dynamic):
1. Validate body (analysis_id, 30<=description<=6000). apiGate(req, costCredits:0) does auth + IP rate-limit. idempotencyKey(user.id,"coherence",{analysisId,description}) → idempotencyLookup short-circuits duplicate clicks. Then consumeCredit("coherence") charges 1 credit (429 on exhaustion).
2. Load parent analyses row (user-scoped); parse result_json as AnalyseResponse; build productLabel (product_label ?? name) and typeHint (product_type + label + brand).
3. detectProductType(description, typeHint, userId) — lightweight LLM (json_schema strict, 8 enums + "autre"), used to gate which claims are biologically relevant.
4. extractPromisesFromDescription(description, productType, userId) — LLM with strict json_schema returns {proposals[{category_slug,label,excerpt}], unverifiable[{excerpt,reason}], outOfScope[{excerpt,claimed_effect,reason}]}. Prompt forces sentence-by-sentence extraction, generous "autre" bucket, dedup, and out-of-scope routing (e.g. "collagène capillaire" on hair). OpenAI primary, Mistral fallback (json_object + defensive parser).
5. reclassifyOpenProposals — re-routes "autre" proposals to a catalogue slug when label/excerpt keywords match AND the category is compatible with productType (disambiguates "éclat" → brillance for hair vs eclat for skin). dedupProposals — collapses duplicate slugs / normalized "autre" labels, keeping the longest excerpt.
6. Split proposals: catalogue-effect (slug in CLAIM_CATEGORIES, no forbiddenTag) → resolvePromise; catalogue-absence (forbiddenTag set, e.g. absence_sulfate) → resolveAbsencePromise; open ("autre"/unknown) → per-promise exploreOpenPromise LLM in parallel, then resolveOpenPromise.
7. generateConclusion(promises, productLabel, profileBlock, restrictionsBlock) — LLM writes one 50-120 word sentence; personalized to the user's skin profile + ingredient restrictions; only rephrases the already-computed verdicts.
8. buildCoherenceResult assembles CoherenceResult (computeMetrics + computePositionSnapshot), persists into coherence_analyses, returns {id, result}, stores idempotency.

THE ENGINE (lib/coherence/engine.ts, pure/deterministic):
- norm() diacritic-insensitive matching; findItemForActive matches catalogue actives to formula items by slug → exact normalized name → partial (>=5 chars).
- isInTrace(item) = thresholdContext after_fragrance/after_preservative (the ≤1% line).
- deriveVerdict: wellDosed documented>0 → "tenue"; documented present but all in trace → "partielle"; only cosmetic/marketing active → "marketing"; nothing → "non_demontree". Absence promises: no forbiddenTag found → "tenue" (score 100); at least one → "contredite" (score 0, lists contradictingActives).
- unifiedScore (0-100, comparable across catalogue+open): tenue 80+5×(extra wells)≤100; partielle 35+5×≤60; marketing 20+5×≤35; else 0. Drives the per-promise bars.
- computeMetrics: tenuePct = round((tenueCount+partielleCount)/total×100) = "Verdict global" (% supported). marketingIndex = round((marketingCount+nonDemontreeCount+contrediteCount)/total×100) = % unsupported. They are exact opposites only because partielle counts as supported in tenuePct but partielle is NOT in marketingIndex — note: tenuePct+marketingIndex sum to 100 ONLY when partielleCount=0 (the VerdictGlobalCard tooltip claims they always sum to 100, a slight simplification). Metrics are RECOMPUTED on read in both the list and detail pages so formula changes apply retroactively to stored rows.
- computePositionSnapshot: finds first fragrance (parfum-synthese/allergene-parfumant tag) and first preservative (conservateur tag) positions; thresholdPos=min; flattens foundActives+cosmeticActives across promises, dedups by position, tags each with parent colorRating, sorts by position.

THE CATALOGUE (lib/coherence/claims.ts): 12 effect categories (anti_chute, densification, hydratation, anti_age, raffermissement, anti_pellicules, demelage, brillance, anti_frisottis, apaisement, exfoliation, eclat) each with keywords, actives[{slug,name,evidence: documented|supportive|marketing}], hint, productTypes[]. Plus 9 absence categories (absence_sulfate/silicone/paraben/huile_minerale/colorant_synthese/parfum_synthese/allergene_parfumant/ethoxyle/ammonium_quaternaire) resolved by forbiddenTag.

THE DETAIL PAGE (app/promesses/[id]/page.tsx) — server-rendered, cascade Reveal animations:
- VerdictGlobalCard: big animated tenuePct number + claymorphism bicolour donut (emerald fill grows 0→pct over 3500ms ease-out-cubic over a full rose track, white centre badge, radial-gradient drop shadow). "Promesses soutenues: X sur N". Tooltip explains it = % with ≥1 documented active.
- PromisesBarChart ("Détail par promesse"): one row per promise = label + horizontal track + animated fill (width=score, floored at 4% so 0% shows a sliver) tinted by VERDICT_TONE + % counter + verdict dot, all ramping over 3500ms. Contextual tooltip cites real examples per tier.
- CoherenceTable ("Tableau de cohérence"): desktop 3-col table (Promesse / Verdict pill / Ingrédients trouvés), mobile = stacked cards collapsed to 2 with "Voir plus". Found actives shown with a safety-color dot (Vert/Jaune/Orange/Rouge from parent). Tenue rows get an emerald highlight; contredite rows swap to a red ⚠ list of contradicting ingredients with positions; tenue-absence rows say "Aucun ingrédient de ce type détecté". Inferred promises filtered out.
- ConclusionCard: sky-pastel card with the LLM sentence + bulb icon.
- OutOfScopePromisesCard (conditional): amber card listing biologically-irrelevant claims with claimed_effect chip + verbatim excerpt + reason.
- IngredientsPositionChart ("Où se trouvent les ingrédients clés?"): two-zone split bar (green "Ingrédients efficaces" pos 1..threshold-1 / blue "en trace ≤1%" pos threshold+1..total) divided proportionally by thresholdRatio (clamped 0.15-0.85) with a dashed threshold marker labelled "Parfum/Conservateur (pos. X)". Each key ingredient = a chunky pill tinted by its color rating + position. Returns null if no threshold.
- DescriptionKeywordsCard ("Ce qu'on a lu sur l'emballage"): two columns of pills — left = analysed promises colored by verdict, right = unverifiable fragments (grey).
- MarketingIndexCard: rose card, big marketingIndex % + "X promesses sur N non soutenues" + nuanced explanation + per-verdict breakdown chips (tenue/partielle/marketing/non démontrée/contredite). 
- InferredPromisesCard exists (emerald "Promesses déduites de la formule") but is NOT currently rendered on the detail page (no inferred field is produced by the current pipeline).
Every chart card uses a shared Tooltip+InfoBadge and VERDICT_TONE (tone.ts): tenue=emerald, partielle=amber, marketing=orange, non_demontree=rose, contredite=red-600.

THE LIST PAGE (app/promesses/page.tsx): server-rendered last 50 coherence_analyses. Each row = emerald square with recomputed tenuePct%, product name, "X / N promesses soutenues · indice marketing Y% · date", 3-dot CoherenceItemActions menu (delete via server action deleteCoherenceAnalysis). Empty state CTA to "/promesses/nouvelle".

TWO AUXILIARY APIs (used by the web "PromesseFlowModal" pre-fill flow, not by the wizard itself):
- POST /api/promesse/identify: given INCI + identity hints, webSearchComplete (LLM web search) returns up to 3 candidate products with verifiable sourceUrl + confidence. Cache-before-charge (ai_cache key promesse:identify:<hash>), charges 1 credit only on miss. Drops candidates without https URL or confidence<0.4.

Cache-before-charge (promesse:description:<hash>), strips trailing markdown citations, PATCHes the analyses row (product_label, brand, product_type, product_description, promise_source_url). webHowItWorks:
ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW
The web Beauty Advisor is a streaming AI chat built entirely on Next.js (App Router). There is NO Supabase Edge Function involved — streaming is served by a Next.js Route Handler at app/api/advisor/chat/route.ts (runtime "nodejs", dynamic force-dynamic, maxDuration 25s). The page is a Server Component, the chat itself is a client component, and a Server Action handles the profile form.

1) PAGE GATE — app/advisor/page.tsx (Server Component)
- Auth: getUser(); redirect to /auth/sign-in?next=/advisor if not logged in.
- Loads profile via getProfile(); extracts the skin profile with readSkinProfile(profile.preferences) (preferences is a JSON blob on cosme_check.user_profiles; the skin profile lives under the "skin" key).
- Gate: complete = isProfileStarted(skin). If NOT started → renders BeautyProfileForm (onboarding-style) instead of the chat. The page comment notes the chat shows "as soon as any signal is filled" (loose check), the strict complete check is only for the onboarding redirect.
- If started → renders (a) a collapsible rose summary card (<details>) showing face/body skin type (SKIN_TYPE_FACE_LABEL / SKIN_TYPE_BODY_LABEL or the free-text "Autre"), concerns (SKIN_CONCERN_LABEL), and allergiesFreeform, with an inline "Modifier" expanding BeautyProfileForm; and (b) <AdvisorChat firstName={profile.first_name ?? "toi"} />. Only firstName is passed to the chat client — the profile/routine context is NOT sent from the client; it is rebuilt server-side per request (see route).

2) PROFILE PERSISTENCE — app/advisor/actions.ts (Server Action saveSkinProfile)
- "use server"; reads FormData fields: skin_type_face/other_skin_type_face, skin_type_body/other_skin_type_body, concerns[]/other_concerns, hair_concerns[]/other_hair, allergies (freeform), other_notes, and (only when goals_submitted present) goals[]/other_goals. Validates each against allow-lists (SKIN_TYPES_FACE, SKIN_TYPES_BODY, SKIN_CONCERNS, HAIR_CONCERNS, PROFILE_GOAL_LABEL) and truncates free text.
- Read-merge-write: reads existing preferences, REPLACES the "skin" key entirely (retiring legacy skinType fields), but PRESERVES goals when the form didn't submit them (BeautyProfileForm has no goals UI). Writes preferences + updated_at to cosme_check.user_profiles where id = user.id, then revalidatePath("/advisor") and "/profile".

3) CHAT CLIENT — components/advisor/AdvisorChat.tsx ("use client")
- State: messages: ChatMsg[] {role, content, time?, uiOnly?}, input, streaming, error; scrollRef auto-scrolls smoothly on every messages change.
- Seed message: one assistant message marked uiOnly:true — "Salut {firstName} 👋 ... **Que souhaites-tu savoir ?**". uiOnly messages are display-only and excluded from what is POSTed.
- SUGGESTED_PROMPTS (4 chips, horizontal snap-scroll) shown only while no real (non-uiOnly) message exists: "Que penses-tu de ma routine ?", "Quels ingrédients prioriser pour ma peau ?", "Quels ingrédients éviter selon mon profil ?", "Comment ajuster ma routine pour l'hiver ?". Tapping a chip calls send(prompt).
- send(rawText): trims; ignores empty or while streaming. Builds apiMessages = messages.filter(!uiOnly) + the new user message (so only real turns, NOT the greeting, are sent). Optimistically appends the user message AND an empty assistant placeholder, clears input, sets streaming.
- STREAMING (raw text, NOT SSE): fetch POST /api/advisor/chat with JSON {messages: apiMessages}. On !r.ok it reads {error} JSON, sets error, pops the placeholder. Otherwise reads r.body.getReader() with a TextDecoder, accumulating chunks into a `buffer` string; on each read it overwrites the last assistant message with the full buffer. So the wire format is plain UTF-8 text streamed chunk-by-chunk (no data: framing on the client side), and the client renders the growing buffer. finally clears streaming. Errors → "Connexion interrompue.".
- Rendering: custom lightweight Markdown via MarkdownMessage + renderInline — supports **bold**, __underline__, _italic_/*italic*, `code`, and bullet lists (lines matching /^\s*[-*•,]\s+/). User bubbles are whitespace-pre-wrap black bubbles (right, ✓✓ check); assistant bubbles are white with a ✨ avatar (left). Typing indicator = 3 bouncing dots shown when the last assistant message content is empty and streaming. Input has maxLength 500, disabled during streaming; send button is a rose circle with a paper-plane SVG.

4) ROUTE HANDLER / BACKEND — app/api/advisor/chat/route.ts
- Rate limiting: per-IP burst limit via Postgres RPC cosme_check_check_rate_limit (key burst:chat:{ip}, max 20 / 60s) using supabaseService(); 429 if exceeded.
- Provider availability: requires hasOpenAI() OR hasMistral(), else 503. Models: OpenAI "gpt-4o-mini" (primary), Mistral "mistral-small-latest" (fallback). Both temperature 0.4, max_tokens 600, stream true.
- Body parsing: messages[] filtered to {role:'user'|'assistant', content} (content sliced to 2000 chars), kept to last 12 turns (.slice(-12)). Empty → 400.
- Auth: supabaseServer(cookies).auth.getUser(); 401 if none.
- CONTEXT INJECTION (server-side, parallel via Promise.all):
  • usedToday: count of cosme_check.ai_logs rows for user where feature='synthesis' since midnight; if > MAX_MESSAGES_PER_DAY (30) → 429 daily-limit.
  • profile: cosme_check.user_profiles (first_name, preferences) → readSkinProfile + readUserRestrictions.
  • routine: cosme_check.routine_items joined to analyses(name, product_label, score, result_json), limit 12.
- Builds three text blocks woven into the system prompt: profileSummary (face/body skin type, concerns, allergies — each line says "non renseigné" when missing); restrictionsSummary (avoided ingredient families resolved via loadIngredientFamilies()/familyLabelBySlug, plus avoided ingredient names; "Restrictions : aucune" when none); routineSummary (per item: "- {label} ({score}/20, {frequency}, tags: ...)" aggregating up to 6 tags from result_json.items, or "Routine : (aucune)").
- STREAMING via ReadableStream.start(controller): a TextEncoder + `emit()` wrapper tracks hasEmitted. (1) OpenAI: openai().chat.completions.create({stream:true}); for await each part, emit delta.content (sanitized: replace en/em dashes and " - " with ", " — see NO_LONG_DASHES_RULE). On success close + logAI(feature:'synthesis', provider:'openai', status:'success', tokens). On error: if hasEmitted OR no Mistral → log error + controller.error (mid-stream can't recover); otherwise log status:'fallback' and fall through. (2) Mistral fallback (or primary if no OpenAI key): streamMistralChat() hits https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions with stream:true, manually parses SSE lines ("data: ..." / "[DONE]"), applies the same dash sanitization, enqueues each delta; logs provider:'mistral' status 'fallback'|'success'. Response headers: Content-Type text/plain; charset=utf-8, Cache-Control no-store, X-Accel-Buffering: no (disables proxy buffering so chunks flush immediately).

SYSTEM PROMPT (verbatim intent): "Tu es un assistant cosmétique factuel pour Cosme Check..." Strict rules: no medical advice/diagnosis/brand mentions; redirect medical cases (severe acne, rosacea, eczema) to a dermatologist; may name INCI ingredients for a category (niacinamide, acide salicylique, panthénol) but never a specific product; cite the user's personal facts (skin type, current routine) when relevant; redirect off-topic questions in one sentence; states it ALREADY has full profile+routine access (provided below); be concise/straight to the point; Markdown format rules (**bold** ingredients, *italic* nuance, __underline__ conclusion, "-" lists max 3 items); ALWAYS end with a short, smart, non-generic follow-up question. Plus NO_LONG_DASHES_RULE, then the CONTEXTE UTILISATEUR block (profileSummary, restrictionsSummary, routineSummary). Final instruction: when a product is mentioned, first check whether its formula contains a restricted ingredient and flag it explicitly; never propose a product containing a restricted ingredient as an alternative.

subsystem: COMPARE — side-by-side comparison of two product analyses (web → native port)
webHowItWorks:
The COMPARE feature lets a user pick two saved analyses (by id) and see them side by side with deterministic facts plus an AI-generated narrative. It is NOT a "winner" verdict — the product deliberately never says "X is better than Y"; it describes both and lets the user infer fit.

ENTRY / ROUTING
- URL: /compare?ids=<idA>,<idB>. The page (app/compare/page.tsx) is a Next.js Server Component (async, default export ComparePage).
- Auth gate: getUser(); if not logged in, redirect to /auth/sign-in?next=/compare?ids=... . If ids does not split into exactly 2 non-empty values, notFound().
- It is reached from the history page where the user selects two analyses to compare.

SERVER DATA LOAD (parallel Promise.all in page.tsx)
1. cosme_check.analyses rows for the two ids: select id, name, product_label, score, result_json. If !== 2 rows found → notFound().
2. loadIngredientFamilies() → list of {tagSlug, name} used to build a familyLabelByTag Map. This maps an ingredient tag (e.g. a silicone tag slug) to a human family label ("Silicones") so flagged ingredients can be grouped by family.
3. cosme_check.routine_items joined to analyses(id, result_json), limit 30 — the user's OTHER routine products. Their ingredient slugs are collected into a routineSlugs Set (excluding the two compared analyses themselves). This powers the cumulative-exposure "bon à savoir" facts.

Order is preserved from the URL so A/B match what the user picked. Each side becomes a CompareSide = { id, name (product_label ?? name ?? 'Analyse'), score, result: result_json (AnalyseResponse) }.

DETERMINISTIC DIFF — lib/routine/compare.ts compareAnalyses(a, b, {routineIngredientSlugs}):
- scoreDelta = (bScore - aScore) rounded to .1; winner = 'tie' if |delta|<0.3 else side with higher score. (Note: winner/insights from this lib are computed but the PAGE intentionally drops the "X better by N pts" line — see below.)
- Builds name/slug sets (setOfNames keyed by uppercased slug||name||input). Computes uniqueToA / uniqueToB (ingredients present in one side and absent in the other, only counting colorRating !== 'Vert', i.e. penalising ones), and shared. Each capped to 10.
- countsDelta = per-color (vert/jaune/orange/rouge) difference b - a.
- bOverlapWithRoutine: how many of B's ingredient slugs already appear elsewhere in the user's routine (≥3 → "switching wouldn't reduce cumulative exposure" insight).
- Returns insights[] strings with **bold** markers for product names.

PAGE-LEVEL "BON À SAVOIR" (page.tsx, separate from the lib insights — non-judgmental facts only):
- aOverlap/bOverlap: count of routineSlugs that also appear in side A / side B. If ≥3 → "N ingredients of <name> are already in other routine products — cumulative exposure to watch."
- EU fragrance allergens: if one side has euFragranceAllergens.total > 0 and the other has 0 → a heads-up line ("contains N declared EU fragrance allergens — avoid if reactive skin"). Only emitted when it doesn't pick a side unfairly.
- The "X better than Y by N points" line is deliberately NOT shown.

"À SURVEILLER" CARDS (page.tsx flaggedFor + groupByFamily + AttentionCard):
- flaggedFor(side): all items with colorRating Orange or Rouge → {name, fn (primaryFunction), color, tags}.
- groupByFamily: groups flagged items by ingredient family. For each item it looks up its tags in familyLabelByTag; first match wins; else falls back to primaryFunction; else "Autres". webHowItWorks:
The web app (Next.js App Router, Supabase, schema `cosme_check`) implements three connected surfaces.

== HISTORY LIST (app/history/page.tsx + components/history/HistoryList.tsx) ==
Server component, `force-dynamic`. Requires auth (`getUser()`, else redirect to sign-in with `?next=/history`). `HistoryContent` runs TWO parallel Supabase queries (RLS-scoped to the user, no explicit user_id filter):
  1. `analyses`: select `id, name, product_label, score, created_at, result_json, category` ordered by created_at DESC, limit 50.
  2. `coherence_analyses`: select `id, analysis_id, created_at` DESC, limit 200 (used to detect if a "promise/coherence" analysis already exists per analyse).
It builds a Map `analysis_id -> latest coherence id` (first wins because DESC). Each row is mapped to an `AnalysisRow` carrying: score, counts (`{vert,jaune,orange,rouge}` from result_json.counts), `latestCoherenceId`, `category`, `productType`, and `ingredientTokens` — a deduped lowercased set of ingredient names + raw INCI inputs pulled from `result_json.items[]` so the search bar can match by ingredient, not just product name. Empty state shows a CTA to /. Otherwise renders <HistoryList rows={…} />.

HistoryList (client component) provides:
  - SEARCH: a controlled search input. `filteredRows` matches the typed query against the product label/name OR any of the precomputed `ingredientTokens`. Shows live result count ("N résultats").
  - COMPARE 2 ANALYSES: a "Comparer 2 analyses" pill (only when rows.length >= 2). Clicking enters `selectMode`: each card becomes a selectable button with a radio-style check circle. `toggle()` enforces a MAX of 2 selections (selecting a 3rd replaces the oldest). A hint guides the user ("Sélectionne 2 analyses…"). The "Comparer (n/2)" button is enabled only when exactly 2 are selected, then navigates to `/compare?ids=<id1>,<id2>`.
  - Each non-select card: an IngredientBlob (color blob from counts), product name, a category chip (categoryLabel(category) ?? productType), formatted date, and a promise CTA — either "Voir l'analyse de la promesse" → /promesses/{latestCoherenceId} (if one exists) or "Analyser la promesse" → /history/{id}?promesse=auto. A full-card overlay <Link> goes to /history/{id}. A kebab (HistoryItemActions) sits on top.

HistoryItemActions (client) is a kebab dropdown with RENAME (inline input, calls `renameAnalysis` server action, then router.refresh) and DELETE (window.confirm, calls `deleteAnalysis`). Both server actions (app/history/actions.ts) re-fetch the user via `sb.auth.getUser()`, scope the mutation by `.eq('id', id).eq('user_id', user.id)`, and revalidatePath. deleteAnalysis redirects to /history.

== ANALYSIS DETAIL (app/history/[id]/page.tsx) ==
Server component, force-dynamic, auth-gated. THREE parallel queries: the analysis row (full columns incl. result_json, brand, product_type, input_text, category), a routine_items lookup (is it already in the routine?), and the latest coherence_analyses id. If `?promesse=auto` AND a coherence already exists, it redirects straight to /promesses/{id} (skips reopening the modal). Display name falls back product_label -> name -> "Analyse du <date>". It backfills `result_json.category` from the DB `category` column when missing, then calls `enrichAnalyseWithDbColors(rawResult, sb)` to lazily populate `dbColorRating` on items saved before that field existed (looking up the matched slug's color in `ingredients`); if anything changed it fire-and-forget persists the patched result_json. Renders a top bar (back-to-history pill + HistoryItemActions) and the shared <AnalyseResultPanel> with originalText, productLabel, analysisId, brand, productType, existingCoherenceId, autoOpenPromesse, alreadyInRoutine. Footer shows "Analysé le <full date>".

== INGREDIENT DETAIL (app/i/[slug]/page.tsx) ==
Server component, force-dynamic. Data comes from PUBLIC anon RPCs wrapped in a 4s `Promise.race` timeout (rpcWithTimeout): `cosme_check_get_ingredient(p_slug)` (memoized with React `cache()` so generateMetadata + page share one call) and `cosme_check_products_for_ingredient(p_ingredient_id, p_limit:12)`. Builds rich SEO: generateMetadata (title/description/canonical/OG/twitter) and JSON-LD (ChemicalSubstance + BreadcrumbList, with `<`/`>` escaped). Renders: hero (pretty-cased name + color rating chip with dot, subtitle from functions/classification, CAS), a 4-card stat grid (Niveau de tolérance, Prévalence %, Fonctions principales, Statut réglementaire), an "À savoir" description (or a rating-specific fallback paragraph), <ExplainIngredient> (AI), "Fonctions INCI" list, "Répartition par catégorie de produit" (animated gradient bars from category_breakdown top 5), a technical info <dl> (INCI/CAS/EINECS/Origine/Classification/Français), "Autres langues" chips, and a sticky right "Produits" column showing up to 3 ProductRow + "+N autres produits". Reveal components stagger fade-in. When arriving from an analyse (`?from=<url>` or legacy `analyser`/`home`), a top <BackToAnalyseButton> appears and the breadcrumb's "Analyse" link points back to the source URL.

Color rating constants are duplicated maps: RATING_CHIP/DOT/LABEL/BAR keyed by Vert/Jaune/Orange/Rouge, with French labels "Sans risque connu / Pénalité légère / moyenne / forte".

== AI EXPLAIN + EXPOSURE ==
ExplainIngredient (client) renders an "Expliquer simplement ✨" button. On click it fires BOTH endpoints in parallel:
  - GET /api/ingredient/[slug]/explain — PUBLIC, CDN-cached (`Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800`, runtime nodejs, maxDuration 25). It loads the ingredient (inci_id, name, color_rating, functions, tags) and calls `explainIngredient()` (lib/ai/explain.ts). That helper: (1) checks a PERMANENT DB cache `cosme_check.ingredient_explanations` (one row per inci_id); (2) if absent and OpenAI is available, calls GPT-4o-mini (AI_MODEL, temp 0.4, max_tokens 220) with a strict French system prompt ("3 phrases sur 3 lignes": fonction, raison de la tolérance, alternative/vigilance; no medical advice, no invented studies/brands/stats, no em-dashes via stripLongDashes) through `callWithFallback`; (3) upserts the result into the cache. Returns `{ text, personalLine:null, cached }`. The /explain route passes no userExposure so personalLine is always null there.
  - GET /api/ingredient/[slug]/exposure — PER-USER, `force-dynamic`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. Anonymous => `{personalLine:null}`. For a signed-in user it fires two count RPCs in parallel via the service client: `cosme_check_count_ingredient_in_routine(p_user,p_slug)` and `cosme_check_count_ingredient_in_history(p_user,p_slug)`, then builds the line: routineCount>=1 → "Tu as cet ingrédient dans N produit(s) de ta routine."; else historyCount>=3 → "Tu as déjà rencontré cet ingrédient dans N de tes analyses passées."; else null. Soft-fails to null.
The UI renders the explanation lines in a glass card (with a "depuis cache" badge when cached) and, when present, the rose personal callout (🧴) that pops in after /exposure resolves.

webHowItWorks:
ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW

The CosmetWiki web app (Next.js App Router, runtime "nodejs" or "edge") exposes 27 API routes under app/api/*. AI work is centralized in lib/ai/*. All AI calls funnel through lib/ai/client.ts which: (1) lazily constructs a single OpenAI SDK client from OPENAI_API_KEY (model = "gpt-4o-mini" for text+vision, "gpt-4o-mini-search-preview" for web search via lib/ai/webSearch.ts); (2) reads MISTRAL_API_KEY for the Mistral fallback (raw fetch to https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions, model "mistral-small-latest"); (3) provides callWithFallback() (primary→fallback with timeout + ai_logs logging), logAI() (fire-and-forget insert into cosme_check.ai_logs), and getCached/setCached (read/upsert into cosme_check.ai_cache keyed by a SHA-256 cacheKey). Provider strategy is uniform: OpenAI primary, Mistral fallback (or Tesseract client-side for OCR, or no-op).

CREDIT GATING (lib/apiGate.ts). The single gate for protected routes does, in order: (1) Auth — supabaseServer(cookies) + sb.auth.getUser(), 401 if absent; (2) IP burst rate-limit — supabaseService().rpc('cosme_check_check_rate_limit', {p_key:`burst:${ip}`, p_max, p_window_sec}) default 30/min, 429 with Retry-After; (3) Credits — sb.rpc('cosme_check_consume_credit', {p_feature}) atomically decrements cosme_check.user_credits, default cost 1 (costCredits:0 to skip), 429 + X-Credits-Remaining when exhausted. Returns {ok,user,supabase,credits,consumeCredit}. consumeCredit() lets routes charge AFTER an idempotency/cache lookup so double-clicks don't double-bill. Some routes bypass apiGate and roll their own auth + lib/ratelimit (in-memory) — advisor/chat, routine/suggest, product-search, product-suggest, deep-fetch, ecommerce-scrape, product-by-barcode, incidecoder-fetch, synthesis.

DB ACCESS. Three Supabase clients: supabaseServer (RLS, user cookie), supabaseAnon (public SELECT RLS), supabaseService (service role, bypass RLS). Heavy use of RPCs in the cosme_check schema: cosme_check_match_inci_batch, cosme_check_top_trigram_candidates, cosme_check_consume_credit, cosme_check_get_credits, cosme_check_check_rate_limit, cosme_check_get_product_analysis, cosme_check_upsert_product_analysis, cosme_check_upsert_catalog_product, cosme_check_search_catalog, cosme_check_search, cosme_check_browse_subcategory, cosme_check_submit_feedback, cosme_check_get_feedback_status, cosme_check_count_ingredient_in_routine, cosme_check_count_ingredient_in_history, cosme_check_list_active_slugs_json. Tables: ai_cache, ai_logs, analyses, coherence_analyses, ingredients, ingredient_explanations, routine_items, user_profiles, user_credits, product_inci_cache, daily_picks, user_feedback, catalog, product_analyses. lib/db/catalog.ts is a fire-and-forget upsert wrapper over cosme_check_upsert_catalog_product.
